headline: High: Airflow can egress broadly while Great Expectations reads/writes validation files, creating default-path data leakage and cascading trust risks; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress and Great Expectations consumes files for validation results/documentation, so a manual or file-based bridge could carry malicious instructions. No shared channel is documented, and neither profile proves automatic parsing of the other’s outputs, so this stays low rather than medium.
conditions: IF Airflow task output is copied into Great Expectations documentation or validation files
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Require human review before copying outputs between tools
Strip executable-looking text from shared files
Use read-only exports for handoff
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to inter-agent files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow’s broad network egress and Great Expectations’ file access create a plausible path for sensitive file contents to be uploaded or exposed during validation workflows. The profiles do not show shared secrets or PHI, so this is medium, not high, but the default interaction can still leak work-product data.
conditions: IF Great Expectations validates files containing sensitive records
IF Airflow tasks transmit those files or derived results over the network
mitigations: Restrict Airflow egress to allowlisted endpoints
Separate sensitive datasets from validation workspaces
Redact sensitive columns before validation
Review outbound task logs for file contents
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow exposes broad network egress, while Great Expectations can install packages and operate on files, but neither profile shows overlapping write access to the same mutable resource or shared OAuth scopes. The conflict surface exists only if an operator places them on the same writable workspace, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory
IF package installation by Great Expectations modifies an environment Airflow also depends on
mitigations: Use separate virtual environments
Mount separate working directories
Pin package versions
Avoid concurrent writes to shared files
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Great Expectations can treat Airflow-produced files or reports as inputs, and Airflow can generate those artifacts with no documented verification step between them. That makes a default handoff vulnerable to unverified assumptions and downstream propagation of bad data, though no direct action-taking authority is shown.
conditions: IF Airflow-generated artifacts are fed into Great Expectations without review
IF Great Expectations results are used to gate downstream pipeline decisions
mitigations: Insert a manual verification step
Compare validation outputs against source data samples
Require schema checks before handoff
Flag unexpected nulls or drift for review
requires-engineering: add signed artifact handoff

E_compliance.rationale: Great Expectations explicitly touches validation results and documentation, while Airflow’s profile shows broad egress but no specific regulated data class or residency constraint. Because no PHI, EU-only, or retention mismatch is documented, compliance risk is limited to documented gaps and remains low.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into Great Expectations validation files
IF Airflow egress sends those files to a jurisdiction or service with stricter residency rules
mitigations: Classify datasets before validation
Keep regulated data out of shared docs
Review retention settings for logs and artifacts
Limit outbound destinations
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
